title: Characterization of a Fundamental, Conserved Structure: The Synaptonemal Complex
content: Meiosis is a specialized cell division during sexual reproduction that precisely divides the genome in half, creating genetically unique haploid gametes [1]. Genetic diversity is promoted through genetic exchanges (recombination) between parental homologs, a highly regulated process requiring homologs to interact [1]. Successful chromosome segregation requires precise exchanges between homologs [1]. Errors in chromosome recombination results in mis-segregated chromosomes and gametes with karyotype abnormalities, associated with dozens of genetic syndromes characterized by developmental delays and intellectual deficits, as well as the leading cause of pregnancy loss and birth defects in humans [2,3].
